summary: Model-bound tool output redacts non-secret values next to token/password keys
explanation: Codewhale 0.9.10 runs tool results through a broad key-based secret scrubber before sending them to the model: any value after a key containing words like token or password is replaced with "[redacted]" and the following comma is dropped. Reading an ordinary package.json therefore shows the model `"jsonwebtoken": "[redacted]"` and `"password-validator": "[redacted]"` instead of the version ranges, while the ACP-visible tool output is correct; the model cannot report or edit those values accurately. Evidence requirement: the read tool call on the file, the ACP tool output with the real value, and the tool-result message in the model request with the same value replaced by [redacted]. Redaction of a real credential, or the model's own prose mentioning [redacted], does not establish this defect. Fixed in 0.9.11 (model-bound redaction narrowed).
expected_behavior: Only actual secrets are redacted in tool results sent to the model; ordinary values such as dependency version ranges reach the model unchanged.
observed_behavior: In 10 of 10 independent runs on 0.9.10, every tool-result message carrying package.json showed "jsonwebtoken": "[redacted]" and "password-validator": "[redacted]" (comma lost) although the file and the ACP tool output had ^9.0.2 and ^5.3.0.

provenance.agent_version: historical release 0.9.10 (fixed in 0.9.11); the unit's install input was re-pinned to this release for the reproduction runs, which is not part of this PR
provenance.case_origin: custom (frozen Case written from the issue text)
provenance.reproduction: 10 of 10 valid independent ABB executions (fresh Suite and container each)
